messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: elevated error rate detected on /v1/generate — p95 latency crossed 1200ms, p99 ~ 4.3s, 5xx rate 7.8% across prod-us and prod-eu since 1789991105. Paging oncall (channel: #incidents).
alex_oncall: seeing it, ack. I'm on it — can someone confirm recent deploys? pinging @deploy-bot
nisha_sre: also getting alerts from synthetic checks, eu-west looks worst. rolling p95 spike starting ~1789991098.
deploy-bot: deploy completed: deploy-id=ci-2026-03-15-9f1b2c (rollout 100%) at 1789991000, commit=feat/runtime-qcache
eng_runtime_lead: that commit landed a KV cache change and a new batching path. Canary looked fine but sync windows may have missed tail cases.
alex_oncall: ok first triage — collect tracer IDs for a few failed requests and check upstream timeouts. Can someone grep logs for 5xx + kvcache
nisha_sre: running quick search, sample:
```
ERROR 1789991120 request_id=rq-7a12c path=/v1/generate backend=runtime-1 code=504 upstream_ms=4201 kvcache.miss=true batch.length=16
```
nisha_sre: I'm seeing a pattern: long backend wait + kvcache misses clustered with larger batch sizes.
eng_runtime_lead: hmm that matches a regression where fallback batching path was enabled for long sequences. Could be head-of-line blocking in the batching queue.
alex_oncall: immediate mitigation options: 1) roll back deploy 2) lower canary / throttle batching 3) route traffic to legacy pool. Thoughts?
eng_runtime_lead: lowest-hassle is a rollback. Route-shift and throttles might take longer to validate under load.
pm_jordan: if customers are impacted we should notify ASAP. what's the blast radius? metrics?
ops_bot: metric snapshot:
- total requests: +18% vs baseline
- error rate by region: us-east 4.6% | eu-west 12.8% | asia ~1.1%
- top customer error spikes: acme-inc, vectra-ml
alex_oncall: agreed, let's rollback first then assess customer comms. I'll run undo and monitor.
alex_oncall: running:
```
# rollback to previous stable
kubectl -n runtime rollout undo deployment/runtime-service --to-revision=42
```
alex_oncall: submitted rollback, watch logs for new pods becoming Ready
deploy-bot: rollback started: deploy-rollback=ci-2026-03-15-9f1b2c -> ci-2026-03-15-8e7a0d by alex_oncall
nisha_sre: starting fastpath checks — hitting /health and a few synthetic queries against new pods
eng_runtime_lead: also temporarily disabling the new batching feature flag in case some instances still running the old code path
alex_oncall: feature flag toggle:
```
curl -XPOST https://ops-api/featureflags/runtime.batch.fallback -d '{"enabled":false}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN'
```
ops_bot: flag acknowledged, toggled for all regions
nisha_sre: metrics update (2m): p95 down from 1.2s -> 320ms, p99 down from 4.3s -> 600ms, 5xx -> 0.5%
alex_oncall: looks like rollback + flag did the trick. eu-west still a little higher but trending down. continuing to monitor for 10m.
pm_jordan: preparing customer notice draft. Short: "We experienced elevated errors and timeouts following a deploy; we've rolled back the change and are monitoring. We'll follow up with root cause and mitigations." Need ok to send to affected accounts.
customer_ops: please attach the affected customers list and window. ops_bot had top ones; can we add request counts per customer?
ops_bot: attaching counts: acme-inc 12k reqs in window, vectra-ml 6k, small set of others <1k
nisha_sre: no new 5xx in last 3 minutes on the rolled-back pods. traces show requests served by previous runtime variant.
alex_oncall: switching channel to watch-only — if no regressions in next 20m we'll close the page. @eng_runtime_lead please follow up on batching queue logic and add a safety throttle
eng_runtime_lead: will open a pre-POC branch to reproduce and add a circuit in batching queue. scheduling postmortem with SRE and runtime eng.
alex_oncall: note for incident timeline: root alarm at 1789991105, deploy was at 1789991000, rollback executed at 1789991135, major mitigations in place by 1789991145.
pm_jordan: sending customer note to affected accounts now. I'll post copy here for review before send.
pm_jordan: DRAFT -> "We experienced elevated errors/timeouts on our inference API following a recent deploy. We rolled back the change and service is recovering. We will follow up with a full incident report and any recommended actions. Apologies for the interruption." :mailbox_with_mail:
alex_oncall: copy looks good. send.
customer_ops: sent to affected account contacts, included link to status page and expected follow-up timeline.
eng_runtime_lead: creating postmortem ticket and assigning owners. action items: 1) add queue length alert 2) add automatic reduced-batch fallback 3) improve canary smoke tests for tail latency
nisha_sre: adding timeline and exporting traces to support ticket.
alex_oncall: handing off to @nisha_sre for next 12h watch. I'll ping for final sign-off and postmortem review. Good catch everyone.
nisha_sre: ack — continuing watch, will escalate to oncall rotation if we see reversion.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: mitigation in place, error rate returned to baseline. Incident will be tracked in #postmortems for RCA and actions."
